propositions: Production Python under src/rebar contains 69 functions with cyclomatic complexity exceeding the threshold of 15, and these inherited findings must be accepted as bounded legacy debt rather than blocking every change.

A repository-level complexity gate must distinguish between allowed known debt (active/stale), new violations (new/increased), and maintenance reductions, rejecting only new and increased complexity while accepting improvements.

The wrapper script check_complexity_baseline.py enforces the gate by comparing current Ruff C901 output against a committed baseline JSON file, computing mutually exclusive counters (active, new, increased, stale), and exiting nonzero only for debt growth or operational errors.

The baseline JSON must use AST-derived qualified function names (scope::path) as immutable keys, normalize to repository-relative POSIX paths, and reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, unsorted entries, and invalid ceilings (non-integer or ≤15).

The guarded --update-stale maintenance mode can only lower ceilings or remove stale entries; it refuses to write and exits nonzero if new debt, increased debt, or schema errors exist, ensuring the baseline cannot silently bless regressions.
The complexity gate is wired into make lint, coexisting with existing Ruff and format checks over src and tests, while production scope remains isolated to src/rebar to bound control-flow risk.
